Claire Bennett. I sit on the board, and this is my first time at this site. And you are?
Luiz. I work in credit and collections. I am responsible for the farms and the dealers in this region.
Credit. So you are the one who decides whether a farm gets the product before it can pay for it.
That is more or less it. I deal with about two hundred customers, and they are a wide range of people. One is a family farm. The next one is a group with an office in the capital.
And how did you end up in credit? Nobody plans that at eighteen.
Nobody does. I studied business, I started in customer service, and I moved into credit in my second year here. I am currently the only analyst for this region.
That is a lot of ground for one person. What is the hardest part?
Timing. A grower pays after the harvest, so I am not looking at this month. I am looking at the whole season. My background is in numbers, but the job is mostly about people.
I ran a distribution business for eleven years before I joined this board, so I know that season very well. We lost a whole year once because we read one customer wrong.
Then you know exactly why I sleep badly in February. How long are you here for?
I work in credit and collections for a crop protection company.
I am responsible for the growers and the dealers in this region.
I deal with a wide range of customers, from family farms to large groups.
I started in customer service and I moved into credit two years later.
And you, is this your first time here?

Right, so this is my third visit to Brazil this year, and I want to say one thing before we walk in. When I meet the local teams, I do not want the tour. I have seen the warehouse. What I want is ten minutes with the people who actually talk to the customers, because they know things the monthly report never says. And here is the honest part. My Portuguese is about four words long, and I know exactly how unfair that is. So when somebody speaks to me in English and stops in the middle of a sentence to look for a word, I am not listening to the English. I am listening to what they know. The people I remember from these visits are never the ones with perfect grammar. They are the ones who told me one thing about a customer that I could not have read anywhere.

People hear the word credit and they picture a bank, and then I explain what I actually do and they are always surprised. I work for a company that makes crop protection products, and I am responsible for the money side of the customer relationship. My customers are farms and the local dealers who sell to farms. A farm does not pay us every month like a phone bill. It pays after the harvest, so I am lending a whole season, not thirty days. I deal with growers who have bought from us for thirty years, and I deal with a dealer who opened last spring, and those two people need completely different conversations. I started here as an assistant in customer service in two thousand eleven. I moved into credit two years later, mostly because nobody else wanted the job. It turned out to be the most interesting desk in the building.
